structured.answer: I'd lean toward Harel's "כספי (שקלי)" track, since Harel is a name I know, its fees looked lowest (0.57%) and it shows 0% shares, but I wouldn't open anything before asking my son or the bank, because I never found the government-bond track and I didn't understand most of the table.

findings.where: Whole page, especially intro lines and column headers

findings.what: Every row has six or more numbers; overwhelming and anxious-making
No plain-language guidance on which tracks are low-risk like a deposit
Coloured rings with close turquoise and yellow colours are unreadable and not explained in words
English letters (S&P) and jargon (עוקב מדד, מט"ח, חשיפה) without explanation
Big return numbers like 24% and 26% draw attention to risky share tracks
'פחות מ־3 שנים' in place of a return is confusing
Returns shown 'לפני דמי ניהול' — unclear what I'd actually get
Page is 16 screens long; the tracks I wanted were not near the top
